Luminous

/LOO-mih-nuhs/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Luminous means giving off or reflecting a steady, glowing light.

The old clock's luminous hands glowed faintly green in the darkened bedroom.

Worked Example

Campers setting up late at night noticed dozens of small luminous specks blinking on and off across the meadow — fireflies signaling to each other in the dark, each one glowing on its own without any outside light source.

The fireflies weren't reflecting a flashlight or the moon; they generate their own glow, which is exactly what "luminous" describes: something that shines with its own steady light.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

glowing: a plainer, everyday word for the same steady light

radiant: suggests light spreading outward, often warmly

incandescent: technically describes light produced by heat, but often used for intense brightness

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

dim: giving off very little light

opaque: blocking light entirely rather than producing or passing it

Where it sits · how steadily the light is given off — bright → glowing → luminous

bright vs. luminous: Something bright simply gives a strong, clear light, without necessarily implying a soft glow.

glowing vs. luminous: Something glowing gives off a steady, gentle light, often without harsh edges.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — lumin-

Root — lumin-: light (Latin lumen/luminis)

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: full of, characterized by

Put it together

Put it together: "Luminous" literally means "full of light" — the lumin- root, from Latin lumen, is the same root found in words describing anything that produces, carries, or reflects light.

Use the root in a new word: illuminate

Use the root in a new word: illuminate: A single candle was enough to illuminate the entire small room.

Root Check

Word Choice

descriptive, literal or figurative

Luminous is most often literal — describing an actual glow, like paint, a screen, or a firefly — but it can also be used figuratively for an especially bright or vivid quality, as in 'a luminous performance.'
